column1: # Targets that may be dark, with the reason — `check-edge-vhost-targets.py` reports a
# dead target listed here as DEV-OFF (a note) instead of a failure.
# The point of the file is that it is short and each line has to justify itself. Rule 2
# is that a dead target fails: a vhost pointing at a closed port is a 502 nobody sees in
# a config diff. These four are the exception, and they are one exception — the estate's
# development box, `192.168.1.93`, a VMware guest on a desktop (`RECOVERY-net-bridge.md`
# §"Development host"), which is off whenever that desktop is. Read the list before adding
# to it: a *production* name that points at the dev box belongs here only if its being off
# is the normal state, not if it means someone forgot to start a service.
# The telno TLD family and the fax staging app run on the guest itself; `telno.services`
# reaches it through a reverse tunnel that ends on the edge, so that target is dead for
# the same reason and disappears with it.

column2: dev box off — the telno TLD family (telno.digital, telno.mobi, …)
dev box off — the reverse tunnel telno.services is served through
